description: Change the Mac's sound volume with the keyboard's volume keys, or mute or unmute it. Use percent for an exact level ('volume to 30 percent' -> percent 30), change for relative requests ('turn it up' -> change 10, 'much quieter' -> change -25), or mute true or false. Send exactly one of the three. It reports the level actually reached, which can differ from the request by under one percent. Not for pausing music: use media_control.
name: set_volume

change.description: Relative change in percentage points, e.g. 10 or -10.

mute.description: true to mute, false to unmute.

description: Change the brightness of the Mac's built-in screen with the keyboard's brightness keys. Use percent for an exact level ('brightness to 50' -> percent 50) or change for relative requests ('brighter' -> change 15, 'dim the screen' -> change -20). Send exactly one.
name: set_brightness

description: Control whatever music or video is playing, with the keyboard's media keys: play_pause (one key for both play and pause, so it toggles), next or previous track. Example: 'pause the music' -> play_pause; 'skip this song' -> next. For loudness use set_volume.
name: media_control

action.description: play_pause to play or pause what is playing; next or previous to skip a track.

description: Scroll the window in front with the mouse wheel: up, down, left or right by a_little, a page (default) or a_lot, or all the way to the top or bottom. If the pointer isn't over that window it first glides there. Example: 'scroll down' -> direction down; 'scroll up a bit' -> direction up, amount a_little; 'go to the bottom' -> direction bottom.
name: scroll

direction.description: Which way to scroll; top or bottom jumps to the start or end of the page.

description: Open an app, or switch to it if it's already open, the way a person does: Command+Space, type the name into Spotlight, Return. Use for 'open Spotify', 'switch to Chrome', 'go to WhatsApp'. Say the name as the user said it ('vs code', 'chrome', 'settings'); the tool finds the installed app. If it answers with options or suggestions, ask the user which one. To open a website use open_url.
name: open_app

name.description: App name as spoken, e.g. 'chrome' or 'whatsapp'.

description: Open a web page in a new tab of the default browser, the way a person does: bring the browser forward, Command+T, type the address, Return. Use url for an address or bare domain ('open bbc.co.uk' -> url 'bbc.co.uk'), or search for a quick web search ('google cheap flights to Rome' -> search 'cheap flights to Rome'). Send exactly one. The final Return is checked by the safety gate; if it refuses, use start_task. For tasks on a site (booking, filling forms, reading email) use the task tool.
name: open_url

search.description: Words to search the web for.

description: Press a key or keyboard shortcut in the app in front. Write keys as words: 'command s', 'command shift t', 'escape', 'enter', 'tab', 'down down enter', 'page down', 'f5'. Use times to repeat ('press down three times' -> keys 'down', times 3). Prefer the shortcut tool for common actions like copy, undo or next tab. Keys that can send, submit, delete or close (Return or Enter, Space, Delete outside a text field, Command+Q, Command+W) are checked by the safety gate first; if it refuses, the action needs the user's confirmation, so do it with start_task instead.
name: press_keys

keys.description: Keys to press, e.g. 'command shift t' or 'down down enter'.

description: Do a common action in the app in front by pressing its real keyboard shortcut. Editing: copy, cut, paste, undo, redo, select_all, save, find. Browser tabs and pages: new_tab, close_tab, reopen_tab, next_tab, previous_tab, back, forward, reload, zoom_in, zoom_out, actual_size. Windows and apps: new_window, close_window, minimise, fullscreen, next_window (same app), previous_app (the app you were just in), hide_app, hide_others, quit_app, mission_control, spotlight. Example: 'close this tab' -> close_tab; 'go back' -> back. close_tab, close_window and quit_app are checked by the safety gate first; if it refuses, use start_task. To open or switch to a named app use open_app.
name: shortcut

action.description: Which common action to do with its keyboard shortcut, from the list above.

description: Type text into whatever field has focus in the app in front, exactly as given: punctuation, capitals, emoji and any language. It never presses enter unless press_enter is true, so it never sends a chat message by itself; set press_enter only when the user says to send or submit. The Return and any line break are checked by the safety gate first; if it refuses, do the sending with start_task, which asks the user to confirm. A line break in the text is typed as Shift+Return, a new line that doesn't send. To write and send a message in an app, use the task tool. Example: 'type hello world' -> text 'hello world'.
name: type_text

press_enter.description: Press enter after typing. Default false.

description: Use the mouse pointer directly, for when the user knows exactly what they want: click, double_click or right_click where the pointer is now, or move it up, down, left or right by a_little, some (default) or a_lot. Example: 'click' -> action click; 'move the mouse left a bit' -> action move, direction left, amount a_little. Every click is checked by the safety gate first; if it refuses, do it with start_task instead. To click a named button or link, use the task tool.
name: pointer

action.description: click, double_click or right_click where the pointer is now, or move it (with direction and amount).

description: Say which app and window are in front and which other apps have windows open. Use when the user asks 'where am I' or 'what's open', or before typing if you are not sure where the text will go.
name: where_am_i

description: Get text so you can read it to the user: the selected text in the app in front (source selection, the default) or the clipboard (source clipboard). If the app doesn't report its selection, this presses Command+C, so the selection ends up on the clipboard, as when a person copies. Example: 'read this to me' -> selection; 'what did I copy' -> clipboard. To read a whole page or email use the task tool.
name: read_text

description: Take a screenshot with the Mac's own shortcuts: the whole screen (Command+Shift+3, the default) or just the window in front (Command+Shift+4, Space, click the window). It is saved where the user's screenshots usually go, or copied to the clipboard instead with to_clipboard true. Example: 'screenshot this window' -> target window.
name: take_screenshot

to_clipboard.description: Copy instead of saving a file. Default false.
